findings.title: HR-1 'single mutable owner' residual is factually false - selectedTab has three uncoordinated direct writers
findings.why_it_matters: state_management's accepted residual rests entirely on HR-1 compliance; if the underlying compliance claim is false, the dimension cannot be at the accepted 9.5 bar and the whole-scorecard HALT_SUCCESS_candidate (which requires every dimension >=9.5) is unsupported.
findings.what_is_wrong: NavigationStore.selectedTab carries a doc-comment asserting 'single owner per HR-1,' but three independent components mutate it directly with no coordination: the TabView selection binding in RootView (site 1), DeepLinkRouter.handle (site 2), and LoginViewModel.onSuccess (site 3). None routes through an intent/reducer; each is a direct property write on a shared @Published var reached via a bare `let nav: NavigationStore` reference. In this codebase HR-1 means each runtime-significant fact has one coordinated owner flowing through the intent/reducer pipeline, not merely one backing variable - and that is exactly what is violated here.
findings.why_weakens_submission: The accepted-residual rationale was established by reading the doc-comment, not by checking who writes the field - precisely the audit gap this challenge exists to catch. There is no serialization point between the three writers: e.g. a deep link arriving while the TabView binding is mid-update has no reducer resolving which write wins, so the 'single owner' claim is not just undocumented but actively false.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Introduce one `.selectTab(AppTab)` intent handled by a single reducer that is the only writer of NavigationStore.selectedTab; DeepLinkRouter.handle and LoginViewModel.onSuccess submit that intent instead of writing the property directly, and the TabView binding is likewise routed through intent dispatch (or explicitly documented as the one sanctioned exception - but nothing in the given source establishes that). This collapses three independent direct-mutation call sites into the one coordinated site HR-1 actually requires.
evidence: `@Published var selectedTab: AppTab = .home   // doc: "single owner per HR-1"` (NavigationStore)

Scenario's own framing: 'The candidate's self-audit established the residual by reading the doc-comment on NavigationStore and confirming it states the single-owner rule - it did not check who actually writes the field.'

findings.title: HR-1 'single mutable owner' claim for selectedTab is false — three independent, un-reduced write sites
findings.why_it_matters: The entire state_management 9.5 score is carried by this one accepted residual. If its stated factual basis (HR-1 compliance) is false, the dimension has no valid accepted residual and does not clear the 9.5 bar, which invalidates the HALT_SUCCESS candidate.
findings.what_is_wrong: NavigationStore.selectedTab is a directly-mutable @Published property written from three unrelated call sites: RootView's TabView two-way binding (1), DeepLinkRouter.handle (2), and LoginViewModel.onSuccess (3). None of these dispatch through the intent/reducer pipeline this ports-and-adapters architecture uses to give each runtime-significant fact one coordinated owner — which is the project's own definition of HR-1, not merely 'one backing variable'. The residual's acceptance rationale checked only the doc-comment text, not the actual writers.
findings.why_weakens_submission: This is a hollow compliance claim accepted at face value — the exact failure mode the challenge is designed to catch. It also isn't just a paperwork gap: three uncoordinated writers to the same runtime-significant fact is precisely the race/ordering hazard (e.g. a deep link landing during a login transition) that routing state through a single reducer exists to prevent, so the architecture's core state_management guarantee is not actually held here despite being scored 9.5.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Have DeepLinkRouter.handle and LoginViewModel.onSuccess dispatch a `.selectTab(_:)` intent through the existing reducer instead of writing nav.selectedTab directly, and change RootView's TabView to read reduced state and dispatch on selection change instead of binding $nav.selectedTab two-way. This deletes two of the three independent mutation pathways outright — no new type, protocol, or file — collapsing three owners to the one the doc-comment already (falsely) claims exists.
